learning_outcomes.text: Defines the typology of a structure for a structural application.
Applies the concepts of structural synthesis and analysis to the project of a set of resistant elements.
Responds effectively to changes encountered during the development of studies.
Collaborates actively in team work planning, distribution of member roles, and orientation towards high performance. Encourages all members to commit to team management and operation.

Values and prioritizes needs and resources in a real project execution situation. Translates long-term objectives into operational objectives. Proposes appropriate and clearly defined goals to the group.
Facilitates positive management of differences, disagreements, and conflicts that arise in the team.

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Carries out individual contribution within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group norms. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.
Develops strategies and methods to constructively solve interpersonal conflicts.
Develops own strategies to solve problems and find solutions. Is able to integrate paradigms from other disciplines.

Shows correct judgment to make accurate decisions based on available objective data and information, in an environment of relative uncertainty. Decides how to perform the planned work for the highest possible quality.
Knows the main inequalities and discriminations that occur between men and women and understands their causes. (Equality).

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve a minimum average score of 4.00 points in the theoretical part and a minimum average score of 4.00 points in the group project part. Attendance to practical classes is mandatory, with a maximum of two unexcused absences allowed; exceeding this limit will result in failure. The course is offered as a single sitting, and there is no second examination opportunity.
